geometry._grid: pairedRings and nestedPairs set each ring's grid (9, 9, 18, 18, 36, 36 round a 10 m shaft): where rock and empty space are cut into pieces of about 10 m. Rooms don't sit on it: they're placed by angle.

_sizes: A room's target floor area by size, m2 (a room type may set its own `area` in rooms.json), and how many rings deep each size may be (PLAN-M17).

placement._note: Placing by area (PLAN-M17). leeway: how far from its target area a room may be to make a snap or a handle drag. fill: the range of a fill room (empty space, plazas, the park), as multiples of its target area, and the most of a turn it may take. snapM: how near (metres along the ring's middle) an end must be to snap. gridNotches: the shared grid ends snap to last (40 notches = 10 degrees).

air._note: The hole's air as a mix over its living volume (PLAN-M16). Levels are % of the air; amounts are volume (m3) x unitsPerM3.

report._note: The local weather report (T-074): flavour only, outside the hole. Highs and lows run from the equator's to the poles' by the cosine of the latitude, colder with height; dust narrows the day's swing.

temperature._note: Each floor's temperature (#393, sim/temperature.ts), all in °C (the UI shows °F by default). Floor 1's resting temperature is rolled per hole from a band set by its latitude: restBands' bands, straight-line by latitude between them and on past the first toward the equator, never above restCapC (50 °F). The starter's band (20-25°) is 40-45 °F, the poles' 0-15 °F. Deeper floors rest a little warmer. Heat is measured against a reference floor, a small hole's floor dug out across its unlocked rings: a heater's `heats` is how far it lifts that floor at full power; smaller floors lift more, bigger ones less (never counting fewer than minCells cells). Heaters warm a floor at their lift a game day each (more heaters, faster); with no heat, a floor drifts toward rest at driftPerDayC. Body heat is per person on the floor (living or working there); waste heat per point of a running room's heat effect. Comfort bands are the comfort factor a home feels by its floor's temperature, the first band its temperature is below.

corridorTool._note: Snaking corridors: a border joins the chain only once the pointer is this far along it from the chain's end.

landingKits._note: What the landing crew sets up before the game starts (T-164). A new game's first hole gets newGame's kit, so a newcomer's air, water and power already work; holes founded later get laterHoles' (their seed kit brings the rest). Difficulty (F-014) will give hard the bare kit, and offer it on normal as a veteran start. The full kit brings a heater for floor 1 (#403); a founded hole's seed kit brings one, set up on arrival (founding.ts). A ring room goes at its start angle (notches, 1,440 a turn) with its target area; its holds sets what a tank holds; the crew lays a corridor along the fronts of rooms nothing reaches, and the shortest spoke in to it.
